first.rationale: With only one experiment slot, I prioritize the direction with the clearest durable, unqualified upside: onboarding simplification (memory_31, memory_86) directly targets the two internal metrics currently declining (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%) and has no recorded retention harm, unlike promotional pricing (memory_73), which lifts acquisition but materially damages 30-day retention and was explicitly flagged as non-generalizable. The competitor's aggressive pricing move makes promotional pricing tempting, so I want to verify memory_73's original record before ruling it out entirely, and verify memory_86 since it's the basis for the chosen action and directly overlaps with the onboarding metric under pressure. I am not verifying referral_incentive or enterprise_sales_assist since they don't address this week's most acute, measurable declines. This choice does not resolve the competitive pricing threat to price-sensitive SMBs, which remains an open, unaddressed risk to future qualified revenue and should be revisited once this experiment concludes or if SMB churn accelerates.
